newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS says aims for same profit in '97 as '96.
newsitem.headline: SAS says aims for same profit in '97 as '96.

text.p: Airline SAS said on Monday that it was aiming for the same profit in 1997 as in 1996.
The airline on Monday posted a 31 percent fall in 1996 pre-tax profit to 1.82 billion crowns and said competition was expected to intensify further in 1997.
"We see a number of factors that can make 1997 tougher than we thought when we laid down our budgets," SAS managing director Jan Stenberg told a news conference.
"Our ambition will have to be to hold at 1996's result."
SAS said it expected pressure on price and revenue due to the increased competition. It said it would counteract this with an efficiency programme.
"A productivity programme can give us improved finances, increased revenue and reduced costs," Stenberg said.
